label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: So I have some news (Dad, maybe sit down)

Ok. Deep breath. I've rewritten the first line of this like nine times so I'm just going to say it.

I started my own business. It's called Fernhollow Photo, it's a real actual LLC, and I work for myself now.

!!!!!

Let me back up.

Marisol closed Rosebud Lane at the end of October. She told me on October 6 and I'm not going to pretend I was cool about it. I shot for her for four years and that studio was pretty much my whole work life. But in the same message where she told me, she also said she'd already pointed six of her 2027 couples my way. That's who she is. Pretty much everything I know about this job I learned standing next to her, and then on her way out the door she handed me a head start. Marisol, if you ever read this, thank you. I mean it.

I know this probably looks like it came out of nowhere. It didn't. I've been planning this in my head for about two years. Remember at Christmas when I said I wasn't totally sure what next year looked like but I was excited about it? This is what I was not saying out loud. Rosebud Lane closing just meant "someday" turned into "ok, now."

So here's where things actually stand, because I know some of you (hi Dad) want numbers.

I filed the LLC on October 22. The website went live November 1. I already have 14 weddings booked for 2027, and deposits are in. Six of those are Marisol's referrals and eight found me on their own. EIGHT. June is the busiest month with four weddings, and the furthest one out is at Wallowa Lake in September, which I'm already way too excited about.

For the big weddings I have a second shooter, Jae, who gets paid per wedding. So no, I'm not running around alone trying to be in two places at once.

And Dad, this paragraph is just for you. HEALTH INSURANCE IS HANDLED. I picked a marketplace plan on November 5 and it starts January 1. You can ask me about it at Thanksgiving if you want, but you'll be asking a person who has health insurance. I love you. I'm still not doing school portraits.

Is it scary? Yeah, a little. There's no Marisol to hand me a schedule anymore. If the calendar is empty, that's on me. But I've been doing this job for years, I know how to do it, and I have a plan. Mostly what I feel is excited, and I'd really love it if you guys were excited with me.

Ok, the fun stuff.

My first booking that was 100% mine, no referral, is a couple named Dahlia and Ken who are getting married at Timberline on June 12. They found me because of the pictures I took of a couple at Multnomah Falls. They saw my pictures and decided they wanted me. I read that email about four times.

I filed the LLC paperwork on my lunch break, on my phone, in my car, in the parking lot of a Fred Meyer. Then I cried a little. Very glamorous. Very CEO.

When I got home Sam had made a cake. It said FERNHOLOW on it. One L. He figured it out about halfway through piping it and decided to just commit. We ate it anyway and it was great.

Now the name, because this is the part I most wanted to tell you about.

Grandma, this one's for you. Fernhollow is the fern hollow trail behind your old place in Gresham. That's where I took my first real pictures, with your Pentax, when I was a kid and you let me carry it around like it wasn't the nicest thing you owned. I had no idea what I was doing. I mostly took pictures of ferns and my own shoes. But that's where it started, and when I had to pick a name there wasn't really a second choice. Every wedding I shoot from here on out has a little bit of that trail on it, and a little bit of you.

Last thing. Thanksgiving! Mom, yes, Sam is coming, and we're bringing rolls and the cranberry thing. I'm also bringing the camera. If anybody wants family pictures while we're all at Aunt Ruthie's, they're free, you just have to ask. Kids, couples, the whole crew, whoever. I promise it'll go faster than the Christmas group photo. Uncle Greg, bring a coat.

I wanted you all to hear this from me here first so that by the time we sit down to eat it's old news and we can go back to arguing about pie.

Love you all. See you on the 26th.

Tessa (owner of Fernhollow Photo, which I'm going to keep saying until it stops feeling weird)
